author.name: Reliability Ruth
author.role: Develops the end-user applications and services that integrate ML models. Handles model deployment, configuration, and continuous monitoring of real-world performance. Employs feedback loops to facilitate iterative improvements and system reliability.

challenge.name: The Loyalty Data Audit
challenge.description: A legal audit flagged that loyalty basket data lacks valid consent records, breaking the legal basis for using it in forecasts. #requirements_reuben# demands the data contracts be fully automated and governed to enforce consent checks before any data enters the pipeline. #efficiency_emilia# argues that manual review is sufficient for now to avoid delaying the promotion planning cycle, though she might accept a middle ground if it does not stall the weekly leaflet.

output.content: {reliability_ruth} pushed for a formal owner sign off on every risk assessment during the deployment review. She argued that without a named person taking responsibility for the sign off, the checks remain loose and easy to skip. A signed off risk assessment gives every later check something firm to rest on. The more sign offs we collect, the clearer the audit trail becomes for the loyalty data pipeline. She wants this to be a standard step before any new model configuration goes live, not an occasional courtesy.
output.reclassify_reason: The text describes a push for a formal, standard process to improve audit clarity and reliability, indicating a desire for more than the current occasional practice rather than a hard refusal or explicit trade-off.
